notes.roof: Main shed fine (the automatic overhang warning is a false alarm); the new stone-cutting shed has a nearly flat plank roof with no pitch.
notes.scale: The treadwheel reads as a square oak-plank box with an axle from the side, not a wheel (Carlton: round things round).
notes.levels: Twice the site: terraced back bench with a stair path, treadwheel crane with a tall mast and long boom, cart track, stone-cutting shed, dressed stone stacks. Clearly different from L2, as Carlton asked.

visual.summary: The big works: doubles the site with a terraced pit, a treadwheel crane with a long spruce boom, a cart track to the road, an open stone-cutting shed and stacks of dressed stone.
problems: Treadwheel (around x14..17 y2..6 z9..13) is a square oak frame: make it read round, e.g. stairs/slabs on the corners of the rim or a stepped octagonal outline with the axle in the middle.
Stone-cutting shed roof is flat planks/slabs: give it a low pitched or lean-to slope with stairs so it matches the main shed.
Reachability: every terrace, the cutting shed and the track are reached; unreached are the booms (x9..17 y8 z11, x4..9 y7 z10), the treadwheel top and roof slopes, which is right.
